title: Equality of the Son and Spirit with the Father
english: They said at his birth: 'Glory to God in the highest and peace on earth.'

A summary concerning worship. We have seen, therefore, him being glorified, we have seen him also being worshipped. Both are fitting and owed to God, not to a creature, just as the submissive saints write. David in Psalm 44 says: 'Come, let us worship and bow down to him, and let us weep before the Lord who made us, for he is our God and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.' And in Psalm 72: 'All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship before him, for the kingdom belongs to the Lord and he himself is ruler of the nations.' What then will those say who assign the name 'God' separately to the Father, and 'Lord' to the Son, while they include here the Lord to be worshipped and to rule and his being the kingdom? And again in Psalm 29: 'And I will worship you, Lord, my strength.' And in Psalm 132: 'Let us worship toward the place where his feet stood.' Paul writes from the song of Deuteronomy: 'When he brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, he says: and let all the angels of God worship him.' And the evangelist says, 'the magi said: we saw his star in the east and we came to worship him.' And again, 'behold,' he says, 'a leper came and worshipped him.' And again according to Matthew he says: 'the wind ceased. And they in the ship worshipped him, saying: truly you are the Son of God,' and not, he says, those called sons by a cheap gift among us. And: 'a certain ruler worshipped him.' And after his resurrection on the mountain he says: 'the apostles, having seen him, worshipped him.'

A summary concerning faith toward God the Father. Therefore, according to the Scripture, saying much more or about the Father, [it says] much about the Son, declaring him almighty, and creator of the ages, and creator of all things, and true God, and not having a God before him, and over all, and a great and above all God, to whom no other will be reckoned, and sitting at the right hand...

Being in the bosom of the Father, and being the eternal life, the true light, Lord of all, only Sovereign and Authority, whose peace has no limit but exceeds all understanding, whose kingdom is unending, who alone is salvation, and who draws the worthy toward the Son; the Father is not considered in any way inferior—may it never be—to His Spirit.

One who theologizes about the Father in such an equal manner ought not to consider the Only-begotten or the Holy Spirit as lesser or unlike. For no creature has the power—only the Uncreated—to do the things mentioned: to create essence out of non-existence, both irrational and rational, to give life, to forgive sins, to call creation His own, to know the Father from equal things as He is known by Him, to be equal to the Father, to be in the Father and the Father in Him by equality, to be ministered to by angels, and for the Only-begotten to be testified as even surpassing these: God, Light from Light, Eternal Life, Truth, and Savior, being everywhere present and all things being established in Him, and for Him to possess the kingdom of heaven and divine peace, to grant it unshakeably to all, and to provide security in the continuous salvation to those who call upon Him.

For those who call the true Son of God and the Holy and life-giving Spirit 'creature' and 'not without a ruler' do not believe in these Hypostases, even if they say they believe; perhaps they do not even believe in the Father. For they transgress the command of the commanding Father: 'Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, O Israel; and I testify to you, if you listen to me: there shall not be among you a strange god, nor shall you worship a god other than [the true one]' (Deuteronomy 6:4, 14) instead of [the truth that] there is never a non-existent or heterousian one; and 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve' (Deuteronomy 6:13); and 'There shall not be to you other gods besides me' (Exodus 20:3); and 'Cursed is everyone who puts his hope in man' (Jeremiah 17:5), that is, in a work of art. This is what the Son says in Matthew: 'No one can serve two masters' (Matthew 6:24), that is, two natures or two lordships; and in Paul to the Romans...

title: Understanding Scriptural Theology
english: The great and small, the temporal and the heterousious fear of demons. How one must intellectually grasp the theologies of the Scriptures.

I, unworthy as I am, have contended with the theologies concerning the only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit, without even in thought harming the unutterable glory concerning God and the Father—for it has not been unknown, even if it has not been revealed beforehand regarding both of the aforementioned divine hypostases, that nevertheless both hypostases are naturally and inherently from Him, the one of the Son by way of generation, and the other of the Spirit by way of procession—but [I am] preparing and setting forth the disastrous interpretations of the heretics, through which they seem to honor the Father more than the Scripture does, and through these they both grieve Him and His only-begotten [Son] and insult the Spirit.

And this is about the same. Therefore, those who wish to engage with the orthodox, even regarding the small work of God—if they dare to say a small work is of God—need words, and works before words, and faith before both these, and much reverence and understanding of the listener, so that through these, having been made worthy to know, even the small is not graspable by the intellect, but is infinite and surpasses even human things—for if it is the work of God, even if it seems small, it is great as being of God: 'How could anyone catch the great things with small labors? An ignorant man,' they say, 'and to will these things'—but much more the discourse concerning the unutterable God, surpassing the perception of archangels, should cause them to withdraw from the unstable inquiries, leaving them to be known by God alone, and with the apostle saying: 'I believed, therefore I also spoke' (2 Cor 4:13).

The theologies of the Scriptures are not to be understood in this way: that when they speak from one person, it is because of the one nature and will; when from both, it is because the personal property of the holy and incorruptible Trinity is being shown; for when Isaiah says: 'I, the Lord, have stretched out the heavens and spread out the earth' (Isa 40:22) and again: 'I am, and there is no other God besides me' (Isa 44:6), it is because of the one divinity and harmony, as it is foretold; when the Holy Spirit is not mentioned in glory, it is because He is contained within God, of whom He happens to be the Spirit; when the mystery...

title: The Incomprehensibility of the Holy Trinity
english: The master, having handed over, says: 'baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' (Matt 28:19), because of the equal, equally-powerful, and consubstantial nature and the clarity of the hypostases. When what is now said concerning God and Father is remembered differently concerning the Only-begotten or the Holy Spirit, it is because of the reasons previously stated. When the hypostases teach differently that the same works perform the same energy, it is because of what is said before. When God and Father has pleased, each hypostasis being able to create and do all things, to sustain all things through the Son and God, and to sanctify through the Holy Spirit, it is because of the single will of the Trinity and the showing that all beautiful things are supplied from it, and because it sends to us thanksgiving and doxology common and equal to itself. When the same names are used for the blessed Trinity, such as 'God', 'Lord', 'Holy', 'Just', 'Good' and such things—except that 'the Father' is alone and always Father, and 'the true Son and God' is the Son and God without beginning, and 'the Holy Spirit' is the one and the same Spirit of God without beginning—it is because of the communion of nature, kingship, and all things. This, however, is upon it alone: when they discourse in secret, because the mystery of the faith is always kept to be revealed only to the faithful. When they say the Father God begat, the Son the Word being begotten, and the Holy Spirit proceeding, it is because of the divine thinking from the hypostasis of the Father as being without beginning and without passion, and having already preceded and being unified, not as near to creatures.

When he says, 'the Father who sent me is greater than I' (John 14:28) and whatever has been thought to be small regarding divinity, it is because of his inexpressible and voluntary economy for our sake and on behalf of you. For upon divinity, neither the small nor the non-omnipresent has place. When the Son says, 'My Father has given me a commandment, what shall I say and what shall I speak, and from myself I have not spoken' (John 14:10), and concerning the Holy Spirit, 'he will not speak from himself' (John 16:13) and such things, it is because of the harmony of the divine hypostases and because the teachings and gifts of the blessed Trinity are common and not different...

Those striving to be a temple, however worthy of the Holy Spirit dwelling in the faithful, as having once received the inaccessible light shining in them, glorify equally—as the Master established in the mystery of baptism—the self-generated God and Father, and the beloved and only-begotten Word Son co-existing with Him, and the mentioned Holy Spirit proceeding from His only hypostasis unoriginally and without distinction.

They do not disbelieve in the consubstantiality of the Trinity, nor do they seek a way or difference of generation and procession; because even regarding the heavenly liturgical powers, He has established this as unknown, inexpressible, and fearsome to remember; and how the Holy Trinity, having itself existed unoriginally, always possesses likewise and in such ways; and how, being seated upon the eternal throne, it looks upon the abysses, and while silencing, hears, and while hearing, remains silent; and knowing the future before the actual; and by word, and even more than word, by the mere will to lead all things; and before one scratches in the heart, it immediately provides the vote upon the request; and it accords all things at all times for benefit; and to be slow for wrath, but ready for goodness; and to be angry through our deficiency, but to remit the punishment through its own philanthropy.

And moreover, it is still incomprehensible how it has one will, and speaks, and provides common things of itself; and it overshadows not so much for the well-being of bodies, but the crushed heart itself. And indeed also this, how it exists invisible and ungraspable by seraphic eyes, uncontainable by word and place, undivided in power, unsearchable, immeasurable, simple, and unyielding; all-seeing, all-hearing, and the hope of all; far more luminous than heavenly light, and higher than all height, as much as cannot be said, and more intellectual by an infinite word than every mind.

For how could the things of the Trinity not be incomprehensible to all, when it is the creator of all and higher than all noetic, and even more so than noetic creation, beyond which is absolutely nothing, and all things...
